item.title: Breakfast Wrap: Intergenerational Report's focus on who we are and where we're going
item.description: Is Australia prepared for the challenges in the decades ahead for the nation? The federal government has just released the latest Intergenerational Report which shows how an aging population is expected to reshape the economy in the next 40 years. The report predicts that for the first time, deaths will outpace births in Australia by the mid 2060s. As the number of tax-paying Australians potential shrinks, the next four decades will see successive budget deficits. This comes as a Senate Inquiry has delivered 11 recommendations in the wake of last year's massive Optus Triple-Zero outage, which has been linked to two deaths.

item.title: Breakfast Wrap: Government unveils digital duty of care laws
item.description:
The federal government has unveiled its proposed Digital Duty of Care, which it says builds on Australia's "world-leading" social media ban for children. The draft laws could let Australians opt in or out of algorithms used to push social media content.

Recap the morning's news, politics and global affairs with the Breakfast Wrap.

item.title: Breakfast Wrap: Can we switch off the algorithm?
item.description:
Can we simply shut off the algorithms sending content to our screens on the world's biggest social media platforms?

That is what the federal government would love to be able to do via new legislation its introducing this week. 

Then we'll dive into One Nation's new superannuation policy with MP Barnaby Joyce. 

And we'll hear about daring heists of food and beverage products in the United Kingdom.

Recap the morning's news, politics and global affairs with the Breakfast Wrap.

item.title: Breakfast Wrap: Germany's far right reaches new heights
item.description:
Exit polls show Germany's far-right AFD party has won its first state election in the country's east.

No far-right wing party has won a major election in Germany since World War Two.

But the party looks like it will fall just short of securing an absolute majority, so will it be able to form a coalition? 

Then - is there an anti boy ideology being taught in schools?

That's what the Nationals leader thinks, so we'll ask an expert who has contributed to the respectful relationships curriculum. 

The Ukrainian President has had a high level meeting with Trump's envoys in Kyiv, the day after they met with the Russian President. 

And the federal government responds to the Coalition's plans to cut the cigarette excise by 80%. 

Recap the morning's news, politics and global affairs with the Breakfast Wrap.

item.title: Breakfast Wrap: How unified is the Pacific?
item.description:
Fresh off the Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Summit, the Palau President is projecting unity, despite the summit being engulfed in tension.

There's been a number of notable absences, also the presence of Taiwans foreign minister, and a holdout over a statement criticising a recent Chinese missile test.

We'll hear from the President, and Australia's climate change mnister who was there too. 

Then the new ACTU Secretary talks housing. 

And we look back at the life and legacy of feminist icon  Gloria Steinem. 

Recap the morning's news, politics and global affairs with the Breakfast Wrap.
